## Proposal: January 15 H-1B Intake Deadline

I propose that we set January 15 as our internal deadline for H-1B registration intake, with later requests handled case by case. This would give us a more predictable review period and let us offer employers a smoother process without changing the registration itself.

Last season, we filed 14 registrations for six employer clients. Nine of those 14 came in during the final week of February, and Rosa logged roughly 11 hours of overtime during the week the registration window opened. Most of that crunch was a product of our process: we currently send the questionnaire whenever an employer asks, and we haven’t given employers a date to work toward. One HR contact told me she would have happily sent everything in January if we’d asked.

January 15 should be realistic. HR teams are back from the holidays, budgets are set, and employers already budget for the $215 registration fee per beneficiary in Q1. The earlier date would also give Rosa, who owns the tracker, a clean six weeks to chase gaps and flag issues before the window opens.

That review time protects both clients and the firm. Registration is straightforward, but errors can be expensive: incorrect passport information can invalidate a selection. Last season, Brightwater Analytics sent a beneficiary’s passport scan two days before the window; the passport had expired in October, and we caught it because Rosa checked the dates.

**What would change:**

- Send engagement letters and a one-page questionnaire during the week of December 7.
- Ask employers to complete intake by January 15.
- Have Rosa track submissions and follow up on missing information during the six weeks that follow.
- Handle requests received after January 15 case by case.

If Marcus agrees at our Thursday meeting, we can prepare the December letters and present the date to employers as a way to give every registration the review time it deserves.
